subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is crowdfunding?
options: Raising finance by collecting small amounts of money from a large number of people, usually online
A government grant given to all new manufacturing businesses
A loan taken from a single high-street bank at a fixed rate
A tax paid by companies that produce excess waste
questions.explain: Crowdfunding lets an enterprise fund a product by attracting many small investments or pledges, typically through an online platform.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation CAD stand for?
options: Computer Aided Design
Computer Assisted Drawing
Central Automated Design
Controlled Aided Development
questions.explain: CAD (Computer Aided Design) is the use of computer software to create and modify 2D or 3D designs.

questions.q: What does CAM stand for?
options: Computer Aided Manufacture
Controlled Automated Machining
Central Assembly Method
Computer Assisted Modelling
questions.explain: CAM (Computer Aided Manufacture) uses computer-controlled machinery, such as CNC machines, to make products.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the '6 Rs' of sustainability?
options: Rethink
Restart
Reserve
Regulate
questions.explain: The 6 Rs are Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Refuse, Rethink and Repair, used to lower the environmental impact of products.

questions.q: What does the Fairtrade scheme aim to ensure?
options: That producers in developing countries receive a fair, stable price for their goods
That all products are made from recycled materials
That manufacturing is fully automated to cut costs
That products are sold only within their country of origin
questions.explain: Fairtrade guarantees fairer prices and better working conditions for producers, often farmers, in developing countries.

questions.q: Which of these is a finite (non-renewable) resource?
options: Crude oil
Wind
Solar energy
Tidal energy
questions.explain: Fossil fuels such as crude oil are finite because they take millions of years to form and will eventually run out.

questions.q: In manufacturing, what is a key advantage of using industrial robots?
options: They can work continuously with consistent accuracy and repeatability
They remove the need for any electricity supply
They make bespoke one-off products more cheaply than skilled workers
They eliminate the need for quality control checks
questions.explain: Robots are well suited to repetitive, high-volume tasks because they maintain consistent precision without tiring.

questions.q: What is a cooperative in the context of enterprise?
options: A business owned and run jointly by its members, who share the profits
A company owned by a single sole trader
A charity that cannot make any profit
A government-owned manufacturing plant
questions.explain: A cooperative is collectively owned and democratically run by its members, who share in the benefits and profits.

questions.q: Why might a small start-up choose crowdfunding rather than a traditional bank loan?
options: It can raise money and test market interest without taking on bank debt
It guarantees the product will succeed commercially
It avoids the need to design a product at all
It is only available to large multinational companies
questions.explain: Crowdfunding provides finance while also gauging demand, and pledges do not create the debt obligations of a bank loan.

questions.q: How does increased automation typically affect the workforce in manufacturing?
options: It reduces demand for repetitive manual jobs while increasing demand for skilled technical roles
It removes the need for any human employees whatsoever
It only affects workers in the design office
It has no impact on the types of jobs available
questions.explain: Automation replaces many routine manual tasks but creates a need for workers to programme, maintain and supervise the machinery.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'reduce' and 'reuse' in the 6 Rs?
options: Reduce means using less material or energy; reuse means using a product again rather than discarding it
Reduce means recycling waste; reuse means burning it for energy
Reduce means using more durable materials; reuse means using cheaper ones
There is no difference; the terms mean the same thing
questions.explain: Reducing lowers the resources used in the first place, whereas reusing extends the life of an existing product.

questions.q: What is meant by 'planned obsolescence'?
options: Designing a product with a deliberately limited lifespan so it needs replacing
Planning a factory layout to reduce material waste
Designing a product to last as long as possible
Delaying the launch of a product to build demand
questions.explain: Planned obsolescence deliberately shortens a product's useful life to encourage repeat purchases, which raises sustainability concerns.

questions.q: What is the main aim of 'continuous improvement' (lean manufacturing) in industry?
options: To steadily reduce waste and improve efficiency in the production process
To increase the amount of packaging used per product
To slow down production so workers make fewer mistakes
To replace all products with a single standard design
questions.explain: Continuous improvement makes small, ongoing changes to cut waste and improve quality and efficiency in manufacturing.

questions.q: What is one benefit of virtual (digital) marketing for a small enterprise?
options: It can reach a large, global audience at relatively low cost
It guarantees that every viewer will buy the product
It removes the need to design attractive products
It only works for large multinational companies
questions.explain: Digital and social media marketing lets small businesses promote products worldwide far more cheaply than traditional advertising.

questions.q: Why do designers consider a product's carbon footprint?
options: To assess the total greenhouse gas emissions caused across its life and reduce environmental impact
To calculate how much the product will weigh
To decide how much to charge customers for delivery
To measure the physical size of the product's packaging
questions.explain: Carbon footprint estimates the greenhouse gases produced through materials, manufacture, use and disposal, guiding greener design choices.

questions.q: How can artificial intelligence (AI) support modern product design and manufacture?
options: By analysing large amounts of data to predict trends, optimise designs and control processes
By physically assembling every product entirely without machinery
By permanently removing the need for any design decisions
By preventing companies from using automation
questions.explain: AI processes large datasets to inform decisions, improve efficiency and control automated systems intelligently.

questions.q: A student designer has a strong prototype but no money to fund the first production run and wants to test whether the public likes the idea. Which approach best suits their needs?
options: Launch a crowdfunding campaign online
Apply for planned obsolescence certification
Switch entirely to manual production
Stop marketing the product completely
questions.explain: Crowdfunding raises the finance needed while simultaneously testing public demand for the product before committing to production.

questions.q: A manufacturer wants to lower the environmental impact of its packaging. Applying the 6 Rs, which action best reflects 'refuse'?
options: Choosing not to use unnecessary plastic packaging in the first place
Grinding old packaging into new material
Repairing damaged packaging for resale
Selling used packaging to another company
questions.explain: 'Refuse' means declining to use materials or components that are not needed, avoiding the waste altogether.

questions.q: A company must produce 50,000 identical plastic casings to a tight tolerance every week. Which production approach is most appropriate?
options: Automated CNC and injection-moulding machinery
One-off hand fabrication by a single craftsperson
Building each casing individually to a custom design
Avoiding all machinery to reduce energy use
questions.explain: High-volume, high-precision, identical production is best suited to automated machinery, which delivers speed and consistent accuracy.

questions.q: A designer wants to choose a more sustainable energy source to power a new outdoor product. Which option is a non-finite (renewable) resource?
options: Solar energy
Natural gas
Coal
Crude oil
questions.explain: Solar energy is renewable and will not run out, making it a more sustainable choice than finite fossil fuels.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Design & Technology (1DT0) specification; New & Emerging Technologies
